content.title: About
content.content: Pecans are the edible seeds of the pecan tree (Carya illinoinensis), native to North America. They have a sweet, buttery flavor and a crunchy texture. Pecans are eaten raw, roasted, and are used in baking, desserts, sauces, and as pecan butter.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pecans belong to the hickory family and are closest to walnuts.
They were domesticated by Native American tribes over 3,000 years ago.
Indigenous peoples used pecans in ceremonial rituals and as a medicinal remedy.
Pecans are rich in antioxidants, especially flavonoids and polyphenols.
The harvest season runs from September to November.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: Most of the fat in pecans is monounsaturated, which supports heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains zinc and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for immune function and normal muscle tone.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols help combat free radicals.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: People with nut allergies may experience severe reactions to pecans.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Pecans are calorie-dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole pecans can pose a choking risk for young children.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Those prone to kidney stones should limit pecan intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pecans can be enjoyed as a snack, added to granola, yogurt, salads, baked goods, or made into pecan butter. They are commonly used in desserts such as pies and cookies. Unsalted pecans are the best choice for a healthy diet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store pecans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent oil oxidation. Discard any nuts that smell rancid or off.
